title: The Morning Brief: Jones to Inter, Messi fined, WNBA disrupted
dek: Inter Milan completed Curtis Jones's transfer from Liverpool for €35m, MLS disciplined Messi for an on-field incident, and WNBA games faced consecutive disruptions from objects thrown onto the court. In cricket, Australia bounced back with a dominant win to level its series with Bangladesh.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The morning brings resolution on a months-long transfer negotiation (Jones to Inter), disciplinary action in MLS and the WNBA, and a cricket series now tied after Australia's commanding performance.
bottom_line: Inter Milan secured Curtis Jones from Liverpool for €35m after months of negotiation, MLS fined Messi for an on-court incident, the WNBA and Los Angeles arena responded to consecutive disruptions with a lifetime spectator ban and a league-wide policy, and Australia defeated Bangladesh to level their Test series. Watch whether the Chicago Sky incident results in arrests, whether further WNBA disruptions occur at upcoming games, and how Liverpool's midfield operates without Jones.
body: Curtis Jones's move to Inter Milan closes a negotiation that stretched across the summer transfer window. The deal totals €35m (€30m upfront plus €5m in add-ons), with Jones signing through 2031. The transfer concludes a 16-year association with Liverpool and follows Inter's rejected €25m offer in June; Liverpool had valued Jones at approximately €35m at that time. The midfielder made 228 appearances for Liverpool but struggled to secure regular starts under manager Arne Slot last season.

Discipline arrived in two sports Friday morning. Major League Soccer fined Lionel Messi after he slapped Philadelphia Union player Quinn Sullivan during Inter Miami's 2-2 draw on Wednesday; the league did not announce the fine amount. According to the desk's reporting, Messi said Sullivan had elbowed him before the contact. In the WNBA, play was stopped during Chicago Sky versus Golden State Valkyries on Friday when objects were thrown from the stands, following a similar disruption at Atlanta Dream versus Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday. A male spectator at the Los Angeles game was caught and given a lifetime ban. The Sky won 73-70 on Friday. Natasha Cloud, a 34-year-old guard for Chicago, responded publicly, saying the men throwing the objects were "weak" and that the behavior reflected internal struggles rather than legitimate protest. The WNBA announced that any spectator caught throwing objects onto the court would be banned from the league and face prosecution. The desk's reporting notes it is not yet clear if those responsible for the Chicago disruption have been caught.

In cricket, Australia defeated Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs at Mackay, drawing the two-match series 1-1 after losing by nine wickets in Darwin the previous week. Mitchell Starc took 10 wickets in the match (6-12 in the first innings, 4-39 in the second). Australia's first innings totaled 210 runs, with Cameron Green top-scoring at 67 and Nathan Lyon adding an unbeaten 32. Bangladesh's first innings collapsed to 64 all out, and their second to 95. The match concluded just after tea on the second day, lasting just over two days total.

The threads across the morning are transfer completion, disciplinary response, and competitive reset. Jones's exit from Liverpool marks the end of one era and begins another at Inter; the WNBA and MLS both acted on conduct within a 48-hour window; and Australia swung a series from crisis to parity with overwhelming performance on home turf.
